title: Reliability Fabric: Project Charter & Sprint Canvas
content:
Purpose and elevator pitch:

This doc is a lightweight project charter + sprint canvas for the Reliability Fabric initiative — a cross-functional effort to deliver a minimal set of production-grade operational primitives, SLO guardrails, and an adoption path that product teams can opt into over 2 quarters. The goal is not to create more process but to define a small set of observable, enforceable contracts (SLOs, alerts, runbook hooks) and a repeatable rollout pattern so teams can ship reliably without bespoke SRE intervention.

Why now:
- Incidents over last 12 months show repeated pain from inconsistent SLO definitions and missing observability contracts across hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Growing number of Dedicated and Private customers increases need for predictable SLA handoffs.
- Small set of investments will reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to restore (MTTR) for common failure modes by ~30% per conservative estimate.

Scope (in-scope for Q2–Q3 2026):
- Define Reliability Fabric primitives: canonical SLO template, standard error-budgeting model, and alert tiers (P0,P1,P2) mapped to services.
- Implement an SLO-as-Code spec and a lightweight validator that CI can run.
- Build two observability contracts: request-level latency histogram and per-model error-rate metric with labels for deployment-mode and instance-type.
- Run 3 pilot rollouts (Hosted API ingestion, Dedicated routing service, Private control-plane) using the sprint canvas.
- Deliver a playbook for on-call and incident handoff that non-SRE product teams can follow.

Out of scope (this phase):
- Full automation of policy enforcement across all infra (will be an H2 project).
- Rewriting existing dashboards or metrics beyond the two contract metrics defined above.

Success metrics (measurable outcomes):
- 3 pilot teams onboarded with fabric contracts in 8 sprints.
- Pull request validator rejects malformed SLO specs in < 5 minutes CI feedback loop.
- Average MTTD for pilot services reduced by 20% month-over-month during pilot.
- 80% of incidents tied to pilot services have an identified post-incident action referencing an updated SLO or runbook entry.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Initiative Lead (project owner): Aisha Patel — overall delivery, cross-team coordination, exec updates.
- SRE Architects: Miguel Santos, Leah Kim — SLO model, alert tier definitions, runbook templates.
- Observability Engineers: Rajat Menon — metrics contracts, dashboards, instrumentation guidance.
- Product Liaisons (pilot teams): Tom Rivera (Hosted API), Priya Das (Dedicated routing), Evan Wu (Private control-plane).
- Platform Eng: review for CI/validator integration and infra changes.

High-level timeline (8 sprints, 2 weeks each):
- Sprint 1: Charter sign-off, kickoff, discovery with pilot teams, catalog existing SLOs and incident postmortems.
- Sprint 2: Draft SLO-as-Code schema, initial validator prototype, define two observability contracts.
- Sprint 3: Validator v0.1 in CI for one pilot; instrumentation guidance for latency and error metrics.
- Sprint 4: Pilot #1 onboarding complete; begin drafting playbooks and on-call handoff template.
- Sprint 5: Pilot #2 onboarding; iterate validator and rules; collect telemetry baseline.
- Sprint 6: Pilot #3 onboarding; begin incident simulation exercises and tabletop run.
- Sprint 7: Consolidate learning, update templates and runbooks; automation candidates identified.
- Sprint 8: Finalize deliverables, exec readout, roadmap to H2 automation work.

Sprint canvas (per-pilot deliverable checklist):
- Week 0 (prep): Meet with product lead, list current SLIs/SLOs/dashboards, attach related Jiras.
- Week 1–2: Apply SLO-as-Code skeleton, run validator, fix schema errors.
- Week 3–4: Instrument missing metrics (histogram labels, error counters), push telemetry, verify in Observability.
- Week 5–6: Define alerting thresholds tied to error budget policies, document runbook steps.
- Week 7–8: Execute failure injection tabletop (simulated outage) and update runbook based on lessons.

Operational primitives (one-line definitions):
- SLO-as-Code: a YAML spec with service, SLI, window, target, and alert-policy pointers.
- Error Budget Policy: clear actions mapped to remaining budget percentage (e.g., >=50%: no action; 20–50%: pause risky rollouts; <20%: automatic mitigation/rollback).
- Observability Contract: the minimum metric set and label schema every service must expose for fabric membership.
- CI Validator: lightweight linter integrated in GitHub Actions that enforces SLO schema and basic sanity checks.

Runbook outline (template to include in pilot repos):
- Symptoms (what developers see)
- Quick checks (top 5 queries in monitoring console)
- Escalation matrix (who to call at 0/15/60 minutes)
- Short-term mitigation steps (throttles, fallback model, redirect traffic)
- Post-incident actions (update SLO, add tests, schedule follow-up)

Risk register (top risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Pilot teams resist additional instrumentation work. Mitigation: Provide a short migration script and pair-programming sessions; measure estimated dev-hours saved post-onboard.
- Risk: Validator false positives slow engineering flow. Mitigation: Start with warnings-only mode for first 2 sprints and collect feedback.
- Risk: Metrics cardinality explosion across labels. Mitigation: define strict label whitelist and sampling guidance in observability contract.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync (SRE Architects + product liaisons) — standing invite.
- Biweekly all-hands lightning demos to surface learnings.
- #reliability-fabric Slack channel for async status, blockers, and runbook links.
- Executive update after sprint 4 and final readout at sprint 8.

Pilot onboarding checklist (short):
- Add SLO-as-Code file at repo root with owner and linked Jira.
- Ensure histogram + error metric instrumented and visible in observability within 48 hours of PR merge.
- Validator CI status green for SLO file.
- Run tabletop simulation completed and notes attached to PR.
- Runbook committed to repo and cross-linked in team's run schedule.

Notes / open questions to resolve in Sprint 1:
- Should Fabric enforcement be opt-in per team or enforced by default with opt-out? (default: opt-in for initial phase)
- Which teams beyond the three pilots are highest ROI for Q3 adoption?
- How much effort to backfill historical telemetry for baseline calculations?

Appendix: quick reference links and templates
- SLO-as-Code minimal YAML example (to paste in pilot repos)
- Validator usage: local lint command and CI example
- Runbook template link: confluence:RELIABILITY-FABRIC-RUNBOOK-TEMPLATE

Next steps (immediately actionable this week):
1) Kickoff meeting scheduled with pilot leads on 2026-03-03 (calendar invite sent).
2) SRE Architects to post initial SLO-as-Code draft by 2026-03-08.
3) Observability team to validate histogram and error metric naming conventions against existing Prom metrics by 2026-03-10.

This doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight — it should be treated as the canonical sprint canvas for the Reliability Fabric pilots. Add notes below as you iterate (tag Aisha).
